title: How video latents work, and each model's frame grid

questions.q: You ask LTX-2.5 and H3 each for 120 frames. What comes back?
options: LTX gives 113, floored. H3 gives 124, rounded up
questions.answer: LTX gives 113, floored. H3 gives 124, rounded up
questions.why: LTX floors to 8k + 1. H3's align_frame_count walks up to the next 17k + 5. The lab prints both.

options: Its latent frames cover 1, 4, 4, 4, 4 frames in turn, so one cycle is 17, and the shortest clip is 1 + 4 = 5
17 is a prime number, which reduces flicker
Its VAE has a temporal factor of 17
It is a rule of the sampler
questions.answer: Its latent frames cover 1, 4, 4, 4, 4 frames in turn, so one cycle is 17, and the shortest clip is 1 + 4 = 5
questions.why: FRAME_PER_TOKEN is (1, 4, 4, 4, 4). Five latent frames hold 17 video frames, and a clip starts with two latent frames.

questions.q: At 832 x 480 and the same frames, how do Wan 2.2 5B and a 14B model compare in tokens?
options: 14B has four times the tokens, because its VAE is 8x in space where 5B's is 16x
5B has four times the tokens, because it has more channels
questions.answer: 14B has four times the tokens, because its VAE is 8x in space where 5B's is 16x
questions.why: Both use a 2 x 2 patch. 8x against 16x doubles each side of the grid, so four times the positions. Channels don't change the token count.

questions.q: Which node's value decides how long the frames play for?
questions.why: The latent decides how many frames exist. CreateVideo's fps sets how fast they play, so duration is frames divided by fps.

questions.q: You want exactly 5 s or as near as the grid allows from a Wan 2.2 graph at 24 fps. What do you type?
questions.why: 120 floors to 117. 121 fits and survives. It lasts 5.04 s at 24 fps.
